items.title: Build by Design: New workflows for new ways of building
items.excerpt: Figma's Config India roundup of launches that bring teams and agents, plus the design, code and context they work with, onto one full-stack creative canvas.

items.title: Design together with code layers on the canvas
items.excerpt: Figma moves code layers into open beta, so teams can prototype with working code directly on the design canvas.

items.title: Introducing Specs: Markdown as a medium
items.excerpt: Figma launches Specs, a Markdown container for context that lives on the canvas, giving designers and AI agents a shared written spec beside the design.

items.title: The AI you already use, now powering the apps you create
items.excerpt: Lovable adds GPT-Live, the latest Claude models, Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini Omni, Lyria and more, so prompt-built apps can include voice, reasoning, video, music and live web research.

items.title: Bluesky's AI tool now lets you make games and apps to share on social
items.excerpt: Bluesky's Attie tool now builds small games and apps from prompts that users share in their feeds; the CEO calls it 'vibe coding for your community.'

items.title: MAI-Image-2.6 and MAI-Image-2.6-Flash now available on AI Gateway
items.excerpt: Microsoft's MAI-Image-2.6 and its Flash variant, for generating and editing images, are now callable through Vercel AI Gateway with one API key.

items.title: Adobe rebuilt Photoshop and Premiere for NVIDIA's RTX Spark platform
items.excerpt: Adobe says it 're-architected' Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D to run faster on PCs built on NVIDIA's RTX Spark AI superchip, which launches Oct 16.

items.title: I ran Blender via Nvidia's new RTX Spark AI agent - here's what happened
items.excerpt: A launch-day hands-on: a self-described Blender beginner drives the 3D app through the on-device AI agent on an RTX Spark laptop and reports how far it gets.

items.title: This game was made with AI in 30 minutes, and it's a bit of a wake-up call
items.excerpt: Dragon Quest creator Yuji Horii built a playable game with AI tools in about 30 minutes, an experiment that makes game production look startlingly easy.

items.title: Epic's delayed Marvel and Star Wars game is going all-in on AI
items.excerpt: Epic says its delayed Disney game will lean on AI to deliver 'MORE and BETTER stuff'; artists and fans are sceptical of the AI-first production pitch.

items.title: Welcome FLUX.3 Image Klein in Diffusers
items.excerpt: Black Forest Labs' open FLUX.3 Image Klein runs in Diffusers from day one: one model for text-to-image, multi-reference image-to-image and bounding-box layout control, about 2s per 1024px image on an H100, with FP8/NVFP4 weights for smaller GPUs. (FLUX.3 Image itself was covered earlier; Klein is the new open small release.)

items.title: Spec-driven development: the rise of Markdown
items.excerpt: Why Markdown spec files have become the working interface between people and coding agents; a timely companion to Figma's Markdown-based Specs launch.

items.title: Designing for skin, not screens: the constraints behind an AI tattoo design tool
items.excerpt: A build log on the design constraints AI image tools miss when the output is a tattoo stencil: line weight, skin aging and placement rather than on-screen beauty.

items.title: We had an AI build two storefronts. Its self-review passed. Its browser QA caught 4 bugs.
items.excerpt: A case study: an AI agent built two storefront sites and passed its own review, but a browser-based visual QA pass still found four UI bugs.

items.title: Hesai launches 3D data engine for physical AI
items.excerpt: Hesai's Kosmo combines lidar scanning with cloud reconstruction to turn real spaces into robot-training 3D environments; a store deployment hit a 99% task success rate.

items.title: AI cloned Adobe's apps for free in design's Napster moment
items.excerpt: Developer Brandon Thomas used AI to build seven free, open-source clones of Adobe's apps; Creative Boom asks whether this is design software's Napster moment. (Off-list outlet: no on-list source covered it.)

items.title: Nobody wants your AI app
items.excerpt: An essay arguing that standalone AI apps are losing to intelligence embedded invisibly in existing platforms, and what that means for how AI products should be designed.

items.title: The synth everyone owned and few could program: a lesson for AI design
items.excerpt: Using the Yamaha DX7's factory presets as a parallel, the piece argues that AI made quality average and that visible decisions now set design work apart.

items.title: Taste is not a design methodology
items.excerpt: Pushes back on 'taste' as the stock answer to AI-generated sameness, arguing that good products come from fact-based judgment and the agency to act on it.

items.title: Config India 2026: Figma product launch keynote (Dylan Field)
items.excerpt: Dylan Field's Config India keynote video walking through the launches, including code layers, Specs and Payload websites, for teams designing and building with agents.
